# Usage

<!-- This file is generated by filen-cli. Do not edit it directly! -->

Welcome to Filen CLI v0.3.0!

You can find out more about the Filen CLI at https://github.com/FilenCloudDienste/filen-cli-releases

Invoke the Filen CLI with no command specified to enter interactive mode (REPL).
There, you can specify absolute paths (starting with "/") or relative paths (supports "." and "..").
The REPL keeps the lines you enter in `repl_history` in the config directory, except those that
give a password or another secret, and those that pass arguments on to rclone.

Without a terminal on stdin, it runs the commands piped into it instead, one per line,
and exits with the code of the last one that failed.

A command asks at the terminal for what it needs and was not given, such as a password or a
confirmation. When stdin is not a terminal, as with `filen rm -p file < list` or commands piped
in, it asks at the controlling terminal instead (`/dev/tty`, or the console on Windows), as git
and ssh do. `--yes` answers every yes/no question with yes without asking, from confirmations
such as `rm -p`'s to "Enable download?", "Keep me logged in?" and the offer of an update, but
not what `sync` asks about deletions it held back (see `help sync-deletions-and-conflicts`).
Questions that ask for a value, such as a password or a choice from a list, still need a
terminal or the option that gives it. `--no-input` never asks. A question that cannot be asked,
with `--no-input` or without any terminal, fails the command with exit code 2, naming the option
that answers it instead where there is one.

Options can go before or after the command (`filen --json ls` or `filen ls --json`),
except for `--password` and `--two-factor-code`, which go before it. After `filen rclone`,
everything goes to Rclone as it is, so the CLI's options go before `rclone`.
In the REPL, a line can add `--json`, `--quiet`, `-v` or `--yes` for its own command.

## Options

- `-v, --verbose...`  
  Increase verbosity (-v, -vv, -vvv)  
- `-q, --quiet`  
  Hide progress bars and other non-essential output (overrides -v)  
- `--config-dir <CONFIG_DIR>`  
  Config directory, created if missing (overrides system default; FILEN_CLI_DATA_DIR also sets it) [env: FILEN_CLI_CONFIG_DIR=] [aliases: --data-dir]  
- `--profile <NAME>`  
  Use this profile: its own login, cache and logs, in a directory of the config directory (letters, digits, `-` and `_`) [env: FILEN_CLI_PROFILE=]  
- `--log-file <PATH>`  
  Append the log to this file instead of writing it to the config directory  
- `--no-log-file`  
  Do not write a log file  
- `-e, --email <EMAIL>`  
  Filen account email (requires --password) [env: FILEN_CLI_EMAIL]  
- `-p, --password <PASSWORD>`  
  Filen account password (requires --email) [env: FILEN_CLI_PASSWORD]  
- `-t, --two-factor-code <TWO_FACTOR_CODE>`  
  Filen account two-factor code or recovery key (optional, requires --email and --password) [env: FILEN_CLI_2FA_CODE]  
- `--auth-config-path <AUTH_CONFIG_PATH>`  
  Path to auth config file (exported via `filen export-auth-config`)  
- `--concurrency <CONCURRENCY>`  
  Limit concurrent API connections  
- `--requests-per-sec <REQUESTS_PER_SEC>`  
  Maximum number of API requests per second  
- `--upload-bandwidth-kbps <UPLOAD_BANDWIDTH_KBPS>`  
  Cap upload bandwidth, in kilobytes per second  
- `--download-bandwidth-kbps <DOWNLOAD_BANDWIDTH_KBPS>`  
  Cap download bandwidth, in kilobytes per second  
- `--memory-budget-bytes <MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES>`  
  Memory budget for file I/O, in bytes  
- `--connect-timeout-secs <CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS>`  
  Connection timeout, in seconds  
- `--skip-update`  
  Skip checking for updates  
- `--force-update-check`  
  Force checking for updates  
- `--always-update`  
  Force checking for updates and install them automatically. Usually, updates are only installed in REPL mode  
- `--reluctant-autocomplete`  
  Sets autocomplete to be less eager, only completing remote paths after pressing tab  
- `--json`  
  Format command output as machine-readable JSON (where applicable)  
- `-y, --yes`  
  Answer yes to every yes/no question, such as `rm -p`'s confirmation  
- `--no-input`  
  Never prompt: fail where a prompt would be needed (pass --yes to answer confirmations)  
- `--working-path <WORKING_PATH>`  
  The initial working path for the REPL or non-interactive commands (defaults to "/")  
- `-V, --version`  
  Print version

## JSON output

With `--json`, the CLI prints for programs to read:
- A command's result goes to stdout as JSON with camelCase keys, such as
  `{"directories": [...], "files": [...]}` for `filen ls --json`.
- A failure goes to stderr as one line of JSON instead of text:
  `{"error":{"message":"...","kind":"failure","exitCode":1}}`. `kind` is `failure` (the command
  could not do what was asked), `usage` (the command line was invalid), `interrupted`
  (Ctrl-C), `terminal_input` (a prompt could not be shown or answered) or `unexpected`
  (possibly a bug, with a `reportUrl` to report it at). `exitCode` is the code the CLI exits
  with, or in the REPL the code the command would have exited with.
- Nothing is printed when Rclone fails, as it prints its own error, or when stdout was closed.
- Warnings stay text on stderr; announcements and release notes are left out.

A command line the CLI cannot parse is reported as text, as are failures to set up the config
directory or the log file before the command runs.

## Updates

The CLI checks for a new release at https://github.com/FilenCloudDienste/filen-cli-releases
when it starts, at most once every 5 minutes: `last_update_check` in the config directory keeps
the time of the last check. `--skip-update` skips the check, and `--force-update-check` checks
even if the last check was less recent. `filen version` and `filen install` never check.
The check follows the release marked latest there; there is no canary or beta channel.

What happens to a newer release depends on how the CLI runs:
- In the REPL, it is offered: its release notes are shown and you are asked whether to install
  it (`--yes` answers yes). If you do, the CLI installs it and restarts on it. If you decline, it
  is offered again after the next check.
- With a command, or with commands piped in, the check runs while they run, and a newer release
  is announced after them, saying to update from the REPL.
- `--always-update` checks even if the last check was less recent, and installs a newer release
  without asking, also with a command, after it. The command still runs on the release the CLI
  started with, and the new one is used from the next run on. In the REPL, the CLI restarts on
  it.
- In the Docker image, the CLI never replaces itself, not even with `--always-update`: a newer
  release is announced with the image to pull (`docker pull filen/cli:<version>`).

An update replaces the executable in place. If the executable's file name contains its version,
the new release is saved under a name with the new version instead, and the old executable is
deleted. The download is checked against the size its release lists.

`filen install latest` installs the latest release, and `filen install vX.Y.Z` a given one, also
an older one (to go back to it) or the running one again, after showing its release notes and
asking to confirm (`--yes` confirms). It does not work in the Docker image, where you pull the
image of the release instead. After going back to an older release, the REPL offers the latest
one again with each check: pass `--skip-update` to keep running the older one without the offer.

Announcements for the running version, published with the releases, are shown with each check.
Update notices, release notes and announcements are printed to stderr, and only when stdout is a
terminal and neither `--json` nor `--quiet` is given. A failed update check (for example when
offline) does not stop the command: it is printed as a warning to stderr, except with `--json`
or `--quiet`, and written to the log.

## Config directory

The CLI keeps its files in a config directory. By default, that is `filen-cli` in the
platform's config directory:
- Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/filen-cli`, or `~/.config/filen-cli`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/filen-cli`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\filen-cli`

`--config-dir <dir>` uses another directory, and so does its alias `--data-dir`, the
environment variable `FILEN_CLI_CONFIG_DIR`, or else `FILEN_CLI_DATA_DIR`. The directory is
created if it is missing. `filen version` prints the one in use.

It holds:
- `logs/`: the log files (see `help log-files`)
- `filen-cli-auth-config.txt`: an auth config, which logging in reads (see `help auth`). The
  CLI writes one there when you choose to after the system keyring could not keep your
  credentials; `filen export-auth-config` writes one to the current directory instead
- `filen-sdk-rs-cache`: the cache of the drive's metadata that `sync` keeps
- `sync-engine.db`: the state of each sync pair `sync` has run
- `syncPairs.yaml`, or `syncPairs.json` as the older CLI wrote it: the sync pairs `sync` runs
  when it is given none (you write it)
- `rclone/`: the managed rclone, and the state and the file cache of the rclone that `mount`
  and `serve` run
- `uploads/`: the records of unfinished uploads `upload --resume` continues (see
  `help transfers`)
- `repl_history`: the lines entered in the REPL
- `last_update_check`: the time of the last update check (see `help updates`)
- `ts_migration_hint_shown`: present once the CLI has pointed out the older CLI's files
- `profiles/`: a config directory of its own for each profile `--profile` named (see
  `help profile-option`), used instead of this one while that profile is

Credentials you choose to keep when logging in are stored in the system keyring, not in the
config directory.

## Log files

The CLI writes a log of what it does besides what it prints, at debug level, whatever `-v`
or `--quiet` is given. By default, it goes to `logs/` in the config directory (see
`help config-dir`):
- `latest.log` holds the latest run, emptied when the CLI starts
- `<date>.log` holds every run of that day
- a file larger than 10 MiB is moved aside to `<name>.old` (`.old1`, `.old2`, ...) and started
  anew
- the files are deleted once they were last written more than 3 days ago, and the oldest
  first while together they hold more than 100 MiB

`--log-file <path>` appends the log to that file instead, which the CLI never moves, empties or
deletes. `--no-log-file` writes no log. `-v`, `-vv` and `-vvv` also print the log to stderr,
at info, debug and trace level.

What the CLI prints is not logged, except failures and announcements. Prompts are logged with
the answers to yes/no questions and selections, but not text answers or passwords; a REPL line
is logged as its command name only.

## Exit codes

The Filen CLI exits with:
- `0` when the command succeeded,
- `1` when it failed, with the error printed to stderr,
- `2` when the command line was invalid, such as an unknown command or flags that do not go together,
- `0` too when stdout was closed first, as `head` closes it once it has its lines, except
  while the command was writing a file's content to stdout (`cat`, `head`, `tail`,
  `download <file> -`), where the reader did not get all of it: `1`,
- `130` when Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP cancelled the command or quit the CLI,
- the exit code of Rclone when `filen rclone ...` failed or was interrupted (usually 130 after Ctrl-C and 143 after SIGTERM, though Rclone may exit with 0 when it stops cleanly), or 128 plus the signal when a signal ended it.

## Commands

> `help [COMMAND_OR_TOPIC]`  
> Print help about a command or topic (default: general help)  
> 🠊 `[COMMAND_OR_TOPIC]` Command or topic to show help about

> `view-html-docs`  
> View the documentation (same as --help) locally in a browser rendered as HTML

> `exit`  
> Exit the REPL

> `version`  
> Print the version of the CLI, the platform it was built for and its config directory

> `install <latest|vX.Y.Z>`  
> Install a release of the CLI in place of this one, also an older one  
> 🠊 `<latest|vX.Y.Z>` "latest", or the version to install, such as v0.2.9

> `completions <SHELL>`  
> Print a script that completes the CLI's commands and options in a shell (see the install lines in `help shell-completions`)  
> 🠊 `<SHELL>` The shell to print the completion script for [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]

`filen completions <shell>` prints a script that completes the CLI's commands and options in
bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell or elvish. Remote paths are completed in the REPL only. Install the
script once, then open a new shell:
- bash: `filen completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/filen`
- zsh: `filen completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_filen`, with `fpath+=~/.zfunc` before `compinit` in
  `~/.zshrc`
- fish: `filen completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/filen.fish`
- PowerShell: add `filen completions powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression` to `$PROFILE`
- elvish: add `eval (filen completions elvish | slurp)` to `~/.config/elvish/rc.elv`

PowerShell and elvish load the script each time a shell starts. For bash, zsh and fish, install
it again after an update, so that it completes the new release's commands.

> `lcd <DIRECTORY>`  
> Change the local working directory, which local paths start from (in REPL)  
> 🠊 `<DIRECTORY>` Local directory to change into (supports "~")

> `lpwd`  
> Print the local working directory

> `lls [DIRECTORY]`  
> List the files in a local directory, hidden ones too  
> 🠊 `[DIRECTORY]` Local directory to list (default: the local working directory; supports "~")
